name: Cuirithir

attributes.attribute: bound with Liadain under a churchman's vow

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cuirithir is the poet-lover of Liadain in the old Irish story of the pair. Their ninth-century poem of meetings and partings is often known in English as the meeting of Liadain and Cuirithir. A churchman placed them under a vow, and the pair lived on apart from each other. The name also serves later readers as a pointer. It sends the reader to the account of Liadan for the fuller story.

okr.objective: Cuirithir is the poet-lover of Liadain and a pointer to her fuller account.
key_results: His story lives in the ninth-century poem of the pair.
A churchman set the lovers under a vow of parting.
The name routes readers to the Liadan account.
